# Native heading line metrics

Original controls generated by `tools/native_heading_line_fixture.py` using
python-docx (MIT). No corpus XML or font binary is included. The reference application opened the exact source read-only and exported `native.pdf`.
`tools/native_heading_line_reference.py` extracts native text origins and
baselines without using the renderer's correction formula. The source,
cases and PDF hashes are checked by the fixture unit test.

The 46 pages cover Arial and Microsoft YaHei at 9, 20, 44 and 96pt; regular
and bold; automatic 0.9/1.2 line spacing; YaHei italic and bold italic at
20/44pt; at-least 24pt spacing at 20/44pt; and exact 24pt spacing at 20pt.
Three sample lines and a following Arial paragraph measure both internal
line advances and the space consumed by the paragraph. Arial is the control.

The installed YaHei regular/bold faces expose 2048 units per em, hhea/Windows
ascent 2167, descent 536 and zero hhea line gap. CSS normal reports the same
2703-unit height. The reference application's automatic layout adds 405 units on each side of this
box. The resulting measured baseline and paragraph-height correction matches
all 230 nonblank native baselines within 0.2pt, across the cases above. Exact
spacing was already correct and remains correct. The independent MS Gothic
controls also remain passing. This does not establish identical antialiasing.

`face-metrics.js` applies this numeric compatibility profile only when
both the family and measured base geometry match. Microsoft YaHei UI,
unreviewed fonts and changed/substituted metrics are excluded. The result
uses the existing per-face cache, with no font-byte reads or additional
per-character work. Font selection, glyph outlines, point sizes and exported
formatting are unchanged. Unit tests guard scope and input immutability;
the browser test checks native positions, package preservation, body editing,
exact undo and reopening.

ECMA-376 Part 1 section 17.3.1.33 (`spacing`) and section 17.18.48
(`ST_LineSpacingRule`) define line spacing but do not prescribe this extra
native font leading. This is measured reference compatibility, not a claimed
contradiction of the specification or a general rule for East Asian fonts.
